text:
meera: quick proposal — want to change SLO aggregation and notification logic for GPU-backed routes to reduce noisy pages during short KV-cache storms. can we discuss?
alex: +1. do you mean change the windowing or the alert threshold?
meera: both. current setup uses 1m snapshots for burn and p95 latency — that's spiky. proposing: 6h sliding percentile window for SLI reporting (p95/p99 by route) and a 3h burn aggregation for error budget alerts.
jon: 6h sounds long, curious about latency sensitivity. which SLI are we using for availability vs saturation?
sam: we should keep availability SLI as request_success (http 2xx/3xx) but define latency SLI separately: p95 <= 350ms for light routes, p95 <= 500ms for large-model routes. saturation SLI = queued_gpu_seconds/request_count (avg queued GPU time).
meera: exactly. concrete defs I sketched:
- availability SLI: rate(200s) = 1 - (sum(rate(requests_total{status!~"2.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(requests_total[5m])))
- latency SLI (per-route): query p95 over 6h: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[6h])) by (le,route))
- saturation SLI: sum(increase(gpu_queued_seconds_total[5m])) by (route) / sum(increase(requests_total[5m])) by (route)
alex: nice. for saturation, using increase(...[5m]) inside a 6h window for reporting? might want consistent windows across metrics to avoid mismatches.
meera: reporting window = 6h sliding for dashboards/SLI export. calculation snippets above can be adapted in grafana using range vectors. alerts will use shorter eval windows: burn aggregated over 3h with debounce.
jon: what's the alerting behaviour? do we page on any single-route burn spike? that's what gets us woken for 5m flares.
sam: propose tiered notify:
- info channel message when route burn >= 0.5% in 30m
- pager if aggregated burn >= 1% over 3h AND remaining error budget < 5%
- auto-scaling triggers and runbook link in alert body
meera: +1. also add a cooldown: once paged for a route, suppress further pages for 2h unless severity escalates to multi-region outage.
alex: can we include cost smoothing tie-in? i.e., convert queued GPU seconds into estimated USD burn and show in daily digest. helps infra & finance.
meera: yes. rough promql for cost estimate: sum by(route) (increase(gpu_compute_seconds_total[6h])) * $__gpu_usd_per_second. we'll store $__gpu_usd_per_second as dashboard var.
jon: dashboards: add a 6h SLI panel (p95/p99), a 3h burn rate panel (percentage of budget used), and a cost-heatmap by route. link to runbooks.
meera: infra-bot, can you create a draft dashboard & new alert rules PR template?
infra-bot: created issue #4812: "SLO agg: 6h window, 3h burn alerts, tiered paging" — PR template in the issue. also attached current svc-level gauges for reference.
sam: one more ask — can we add a per-tenant weight to error budget calc so big customers don't cause constant paging? maybe scale error budget contribution by committed capacity.
meera: good point. add a tenant_weight label to requests_total and use weight in rollup: sum(weighted_errors)/sum(weights). I'll draft changes to prometheus relabel rules.
alex: timeline?
meera: plan: draft PR with prometheus queries + grafana dashboard this week, run for 2 weeks in shadow mode (no paging), evaluate noise drop and missed incidents, then flip to live.
jon: okay. if shadow shows missed incidents for legitimate issues, we can relax thresholds.
sam: ack. I'll update runbooks to include new saturation SLI doc and paging matrix.
meera: thanks all — sharing PR link once ready :thumbsup:
